rationale: This is a single-denominator swap on the archive winner (at → lct in the quality leg) using a ratio already deployed in GrossProfitCoverageOfNearTermClaims, so despite the coherent "common-denominator coverage" framing it is a near-cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Repurposing the weakest-link score as a non-negative conditioning intensity and letting a centered multi-year gross-profitability trend supply the sign is a genuine state×direction interaction with internally consistent sign logic, though it will need to be checked against a plain profitability-trend baseline to prove the conditioning adds anything.

This differs from the archive's MarginRepairUnderLiquidityStress only by swapping lt→lct and DELTA(1)→TREND(3), which is a horizon/scaling tweak of an already-tested channel rather than a new economic mechanism.

The construction and expected negative sign are internally consistent and the change-on-change design is orthogonal to the archive's level composites, but the distress leg (scaled change in working capital) is essentially the working-capital accruals anomaly, so the test must demonstrate that the margin-decay interaction adds incremental power beyond a plain accruals sort.

The within-firm liquidity axis is a legitimately new information dimension for this archive, but because the RANK leg is non-negative the signal is mechanically a reweighted gross-profitability premium and risks rediscovering Novy-Marx unless the depletion interaction is shown to matter on its own.

A plain sum of two industry-standardized, individually well-known premia (cash-to-current-liabilities and gross profitability) is too trivial to count as a cross-theme signal and is best run as an offline control regression rather than consuming an evaluation slot.
